sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's domestic digital adoption and government e-procurement mandates are creating durable revenue visibility for local tech players like 2303 and 2308, decoupling them from US sentiment swings.
Cloud and SaaS migration in Southeast Asia, led by enterprise demand from financial services and logistics, underpins sustained growth for MORA and TCS despite near-term volatility.
US-listed tech (NOW, AMZN, WDAY) remains hostage to rate-cut timing and AI capex cycles, so Indonesian investors must treat these as high-beta hedges rather than core holdings.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesia tech exposure on the 2303/2308 strength, but cap new positions until the US-listed drag (NOW, AMZN) stabilizes; rotate into local names with earnings catalysts like MORA and TCS, and use WDAY's pullback as a tactical entry only if you can hedge US beta.

themes: Small/mid-cap financials are outperforming large banks as domestic credit demand and retail lending recover, driving disproportionate earnings leverage.
Finance companies (GSMF, BFIN) benefit from resilient consumer financing and lower funding costs as Bank Indonesia holds rates, supporting net interest margins.
Digital banking and fintech partnerships (BCIC, XCIS) are structurally expanding addressable markets, with regulatory tailwinds for financial inclusion sustaining growth.
sectors.ai: Buy selective exposure to Indonesia financials on strength in small/mid-cap lenders (XCIS, INPC, BCIC) and finance firms (GSMF, BFIN), while large banks lag. Momentum is broad but not overheated; add on dips toward +0.26% aggregate. Favor names with domestic loan growth and digital adoption, avoid chasing TRIM/BGTG after sharp runs.

Nickel downstreaming policy (smelter quotas, RKAB approvals) continues to reprice equities as integrated players capture higher value-add versus raw ore exporters.
Energy transition capex in geothermal and solar is accelerating under the new government's energy security push, creating a durable catalyst for smaller listed contractors and equipment suppliers.
sectors.ai: Buy selective exposure to coal and nickel names showing volume-driven momentum (LABA, ALKA, RMKO) while rotating out of laggards; the sector's relative strength vs US and normal signal supports adding on dips, but cap position sizes given single-day spikes.

themes: Indonesia's Just Energy Transition Partnership (JETP) funding is accelerating utility-scale solar and geothermal projects, creating durable demand for local EPC and component suppliers like HGII and K

US renewables face headwinds from high interest rates and policy uncertainty, prompting capital rotation into Indonesian climate-tech equities with higher growth visibility and local currency tailwind
sectors.ai: Buy dips in Indonesian renewables leaders (HGII, VKTR) as domestic policy tailwinds and EV adoption outpace US weakness; rotate out of US-exposed names (AWK, 051910) into local champions with strong order books. sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG

Beer and glass sub-sectors (BEER, AMMS) benefit from structural tourism recovery and premiumization, offering repeatable growth beyond this squeeze.
US-linked consumer demand (+0.66%) provides a hedge for Indonesian exporters, but local purchasing power remains the swing factor for mass-market staples.
sectors.ai: Buy selective small-cap FMCG names riding the IDX momentum wave, but lock gains fast—this is a liquidity-driven squeeze, not fundamentals. Rotate into BEER and AMMS for beer/glass exposure with volume confirmation; avoid chasing SSTM/BIKE at +25% without earnings proof. Trim into strength by Friday, keep core in staples with US-linked demand.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Indonesia's island-archipelago structure locks in structural demand for inter-island shipping, making domestic logistics a durable compounder independent of global trade cycles.
Government push on downstream mineral processing (nickel, bauxite) permanently raises inland and port haulage volumes, benefiting operators with mining-linked contracts like HATM and BLTA.
E-commerce penetration in tier-2/3 cities is still early, sustaining double-digit parcel growth that directly feeds last-mile and container logistics players such as SHIP and WINS.
sectors.ai: Buy logistics selectively on domestic-volume names (PPGL, SHIP) as port throughput and e-commerce parcel growth reaccelerate; avoid US-exposed operators where tariff noise caps upside. Rotate into SAFE/HATM for cold-chain and mining haulage leverage. Trim TCPI after its run; add WINS on consolidation upside.

Layer-2 scaling networks (MNT) are capturing institutional settlement flows as Ethereum gas costs stay elevated, a multi-year structural shift.
Indonesian retail crypto adoption is rising on younger demographics and stablecoin usage for remittances, making local compliance-friendly tokens structurally bid.
